'''''Paliurus spina-christi''''', commonly known as '''Jerusalem thorn''', '''garland thorn''', '''Christ's thorn''', or '''crown of thorns''', is a species of ''[[Paliurus]]'' native to the northern [[Mediterranean region]], [[Southwest Asia]] and [[Central Asia]], from [[Spain]] and southern [[France]] east to [[Afghanistan]] and [[Tajikistan]].<ref name="POWO">{{cite web | title=''Paliurus spina-christi'' Mill. | website=Plants of the World Online | url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:717707-1 | access-date=2026-01-29}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Casavecchia |first1=Simona |last2=Biscotti |first2=Nello |last3=Pesaresi |first3=Simone |last4=Biondi |first4=Edoardo |date=2015-07-01 |title=The Paliurus spina-christi dominated vegetation in Europe |url=https://doi.org/10.1515/biolog-2015-0100 |journal=Biologia |language=en |volume=70 |issue=7 |pages=879–892 |doi=10.1515/biolog-2015-0100 |bibcode=2015Biolg..70..879C |s2cid=90939997 |issn=1336-9563|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Description==
It is a [[deciduous]] [[shrub]] or small [[tree]] growing to 3–4 m tall. The shoots are zig-zagged, with a [[leaf]] and two [[stipule|stipular]] [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|spines]] (one straight, one curved) on the outside of each kink. The [[leaf|leaves]] are oval, 2–5 cm long and 1–4 cm broad, glossy green, with an entire margin. The [[fruit]] is a dry woody nutlet centred in a circular wing 2–3.5 cm in diameter.<ref name=rushforth>{{cite book |last=Rushforth |first= K. |year=1999 |title=Trees of Britain and Europe |publisher=Collins |isbn=0-00-220013-9 |pages=867–868}}</ref>

==Etymology==
As suggested by the Latin name, the spiny branches of this shrub were thought to be used to make the [[crown of thorns]] placed on [[Jesus]]' head before his crucifixion.<ref name=rushforth/> ''[[Ziziphus spina-christi]]'', the Christ's thorn jujube, is also identified as being used for the crown of thorns.

==Uses==
It is viewed as an ornamental curiosity, grown for its odd-looking [[Discobolus|discus]]-like fruit, and is cultivated in some areas outside its native range, including western Europe north to Great Britain.<ref name=rushforth/>

It is locally [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in northwestern Africa, northern India, Hungary, and in the United States in Texas.<ref name="POWO"/><ref>{{Cite journal |last=O'Kennon |first=Robert J. |date=1991 |title=Paliurus spina-christi (Rhamnaceae) New for North America in Texas |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/41961083 |journal=SIDA, Contributions to Botany |volume=14 |issue=4 |pages=606–609 |jstor=41961083 |issn=0036-1488}}</ref>
